Replacement Inside Quotes

Source: R/intern_.in_quotes_replacement.R
dot-in_quotes_replacement.Rd

Replace each match of a pattern located between quotes (string literals and backquoted names of R code) by a replacement of the same length, and return the positions of the replacements.

Usage

.in_quotes_replacement(
  string,
  pattern,
  no_regex_pattern,
  replacement,
  perl,
  lib_path,
  error_text
)

Arguments

string

Single string, for instance R code, with lines separated by "\n".

pattern

Single string: regex matching a single character, like "\\(".

no_regex_pattern

Single string: the character matched by pattern, without regex escape, like "(". Used to check the replaced characters.

replacement

Single string replacing each match of pattern between quotes. Must have the same number of characters as no_regex_pattern. Not a regex.

perl

Single logical value. Use Perl regex in pattern?

lib_path

Vector of character strings or NULL: the lib_path value of the calling exported function, only passed on to arg_check(). No default value.

error_text

Single character string added to the error messages to name the calling functions (embed_error_text of the calling function). NULL is converted into "". No default value.

Value

A list containing:

  • string: string with the matches of pattern between quotes replaced by replacement.

  • pos: vector of the positions of the replaced matches. NULL if no match is between quotes. In that case, string is identical to the input string.

Details

string is read from left to right, as the R parser reads code: a quote (", ' or `) opens a quoted part that only the same quote closes, a backslash inside quotes escapes the next character (e.g., \" or \\), a raw string (e.g., r"(...)" or R"--[...]--") is only closed by its own closing delimiter, # outside quotes starts a comment, up to the end of the line, and the %...% operators are skipped. Thus, an apostrophe inside double quotes ("it's"), or a double quote inside simple quotes, opens nothing. A quoted part that is not closed goes up to the end of string. The matches inside comments are not replaced.

Only the content of a quoted part is replaced, never its quotes or the delimiters of a raw string, so that the output string can be passed again to the function (e.g., to replace ( after )).

Warnings:

  • pattern must match a single character.

  • requires saferDev::arg_check.

  • In the safer Backbone section "######## check of the required functions from the required packages", add also saferDev::arg_check when checking for the presence of .in_quotes_replacement.
